About OKNAHRA

Serving the HR backbone of Oklahoma's tribal nations

OKNAHRA is an Oklahoma nonprofit corporation organized under Section 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code — self-governing, non-commercial, and nonpartisan, built to strengthen HR practice across Oklahoma's tribal governments and tribal enterprises.

Our Purpose

To engage in lawful activity in support of HR professionals working with or for Oklahoma tribal nations and tribal enterprises, consistent with our nonprofit, nonpartisan charter.

Governance

Governed by a Board of Directors of no fewer than seven and no more than fifteen members, elected annually by the membership at the OKNAHRA biannual Summit or by electronic poll.

Our Bylaws

Read the full 2025 Bylaws (PDF) for details on membership classes, board structure, and standing committees.

Ruth Reagan, MBA, SPHR, SHRM-CP, THRP, TMP

President

Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Reagan Strategic Solutions

Dr. Lacee Reynolds

Treasurer

Chief of Staff, Osage Minerals Council

Read bio

Dr. Lacee Reynolds, a citizen of the Osage Nation, has served as Chief of Staff for the Osage Minerals Council since 2014. Her work spans financial administration, budgeting, auditing, and organizational operations, including staff management, developing job descriptions, and addressing personnel matters, along with supporting the governance of an elected council.

Lacee holds a Doctor of Business Administration in Management from Oklahoma Wesleyan University, an MBA with an emphasis in Accounting from Southeastern Oklahoma State University, and a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration from Rogers State University. She is also pursuing CPA licensure in Oklahoma. She has completed Harvard’s Tribal Innovation Labs program and the Indigenous Leadership Academy, and is currently participating in the Indigenous Data Champions Fellowship.

Throughout her career, Lacee has come to deeply value the people who keep tribal organizations running, and she understands how much it matters to give them the tools, support, and opportunities to succeed. She believes thriving tribal organizations begin with knowledgeable, well-supported people, and she is proud to bring that conviction to her service on OKNAHRA’s board.

Angela Bunner, M.Ed, SHRM-CP, THRP, TMP

VP, Membership

Employee Relations Manager, Muscogee Nation Gaming Enterprises

Read bio

Angela is proud citizen of the Muscogee Nation, daughter of the Bird Clan and member of Thlopthlocco Tribal Town. She serves as the Employee Relations Manager for Muscogee Nation Gaming Enterprises (MNGE) where she is dedicated to fostering a workplace culture that emphasizes fairness, accountability, consistency, and a commitment to maintaining a work environment where team members feel valued and respected. With more than 11 years of experience in HR, Angela brings extensive knowledge and expertise on a wide range of employment matters, including disciplinary actions, team member grievances, formal complaints, harassment investigations, and allegations of workplace misconduct.

Angela holds the Society for Human Resource Management Certified Professional (SHRM-CP) credential.

She earned her bachelor’s degree in education from Oklahoma State University and her Master of Education from the University of Kansas. Committed to continuous learning and professional excellence, she has completed distinguished educational programs, earning certificates in Leadership Excellence in Management Development from Harvard University and Diversity and the National Interest from the University of Oxford. She has also been recognized as a Workplace Mental Health Ally through SHRM and holds both the Tribal HR Professional (THRP) and Tribal Management Professional (TMP) Certifications through NNAHRA.

Angela is a proud alumna of the 2021 American Indian Chamber of Commerce of Oklahoma (AICCO) Leadership Native Oklahoma Program. In recognition of her professional accomplishments and leadership potential, she was honored as a 2013 Native American 40 Under 40 award recipient by the National Center for American Indian in Enterprise Development (NCAIED).

Drewe Hansen

Vice President, Legislative Affairs

Strategic Human Resources Management Consultant, Strehan Solutions

Read bio

Drewe is a Cherokee Nation citizen with lifelong roots in the Osage Nation Reservation, bringing over 14 years of leadership experience to complex HR and governance challenges in businesses across Indian Country. Partnering with executive teams, he architects customized workforce solutions; leads sensitive, high-complexity workplace investigations; and manages intricate regulatory compliance and employment relation matters, including those rising to the level of the EEOC. Drewe holds a Master's of Science in Human Resource Management, a Master's of Business Administration, and a Master's of Science in Nursing; he is currently a Juris Doctor Candidate at Mitchell Hamline School of Law specializing in Native American law, business law, and conflict resolution theory. As a SHRM Senior Certified Professional and holder of multiple advanced certifications in ethics, healthcare compliance, and corporate leadership, he combines his systems-level board governance experience with his role as an HR Management consultant and Tribal college adjunct instructor to champion practical, community-first leadership and Tribal sovereignty.
